correctness.rationale: A connected feasible design exists (uniform cross edges), and tr(L restricted to the mean-zero space)^(-1) diverges on approach to a disconnected design. The trace-inverse Hessian in any nonzero symmetric direction is twice a squared Frobenius norm; off-diagonals recover independently chosen weights, so the global solution is unique and invariant under within-part permutations. The weighted spectral branches are U=px+qz, V=qy+pz and Nz with multiplicities p−1,q−1,1. At x=y=0 the larger part's per-budget marginal test binds first, at t_on=2p/(qH). For y=0, equality of the larger internal and cross marginals gives (U/z)^2=2D1/(tH_q); x>0 requires U/z>q, and the smaller part's inactive marginal requires U/z≤p. These crossings are t_on and t_fill; hence y is still zero at t_fill. With both parts active, U=V and (U/z)^2=2ND2/t, feasible precisely for U/z>p. Substitution in the budget gives the conductances; reciprocal minimization under a linear budget by Cauchy–Schwarz gives the stated total-resistance values, including the factor N. The matching spectral ratios at boundaries imply continuity, p=q merges the crossings, and leading powers give the fixed-q limits. The frozen exact-rational script was inspected, not executed, and is ancillary to the universal argument.

evidence: Ghosh–Boyd–Saberi p. 1186 gives the convex allocation framework; §V, p. 1193 treats cliques joined by a single bridge. Tovar et al. include linear conductance cost in broader power-budget models. Bhoite et al. fix a base graph and use exact-cardinality augmentation.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general optimization principles permit deriving the target once the new spectral branches and their competing marginal constraints are solved; the explicit antecedent models do not characterize the same active sets.

evidence: For p=q=m, f/m−1 in the target simplifies to 2√(m/t−(m−1))−1, precisely the matching record's b_R/a_R. A single-bridge barbell and an all-chords-absent criterion on a tree cannot account for the interacting qz and pz spectral shifts of two differently sized groups.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: There is actual balanced-case identity, not merely a similar threshold. It does not imply positivity of one and only one internal class when p>q, nor its price interval or objective in that interval.

evidence: Total resistance, mean pairwise resistance and tr(L+) differ by fixed positive factors for a given vertex count. The equal-size Resultary theorem uses exactly the same objective and price pattern. The D-optimal two-block record instead optimizes the weighted spanning-tree determinant.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Changing total to mean or Kirchhoff index cannot make an otherwise identical result new. Minimizing a sum of reciprocal positive eigenvalues is not maximizing their product; the equal-size restriction also removes the one-internal-part phase.

evidence: Resultary da6bd4b37466 explicitly gives the balanced cutoff 4m/(4m−3), exact weights, objective value and uniqueness. The tree-backbone, pineapple and clique-bouquet records treat different support constraints; the two-block D-optimal record changes the objective.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The balanced case is demonstrably covered, regardless of date. None of these statements gives both unequal-size price transitions for the resistance objective.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the unequal-size full phase diagram, in particular the larger-part-only interval with its second threshold. The exact equal-size specialization is separately covered and is not credited as distinct. Foundational convex allocation and general linear-budget optimality also are not claimed as new.
residual_risks: An uninspected specialization of linear-cost resistance allocation could cover the unequal-size theorem. Neither limited indexing nor an unsuccessful keyword search proves absence. The dates of the indexed comparisons are not determinations of priority.

value.rationale: For a natural design model, two explicit marginal transitions decide which edges can be dropped without sacrificing the global optimum. The unequal-size interval is not a guessed symmetric design: strict convexity certifies that asymmetric competitors cannot tie. The support law and exact weights are more useful than a generic convex program or the already covered balanced case.
